question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` now, and what peer identity, authorization, replay, and session-ownership contract must that support require?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses Gateway, session-state, message-delivery, and credential trust boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API, config surface, or security model.

options.title: Design the trust contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and align the linked PR with a maintainer-approved peer identity, scope, replay/idempotency, transcript ownership, and delivery contract before merge.

options.title: Advance the linked narrow PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/43656 as the implementation path only after conflicts, security review, upgrade behavior, and real multi-gateway proof are resolved.

options.title: Defer native core support
options.body: Document plugin, MCP, channel, or operator-run bridge patterns if maintainers decide cross-gateway routing should remain outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Design the trust contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and align the linked PR with a maintainer-approved peer identity, scope, replay/idempotency, transcript ownership, and delivery contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history across session tools and Gateway trust-boundary work, and is the best available routing owner for the product/security decision.
